title: Independent density and coherence skin effects in adaptive fermion circuits
authors: Karim Chahine, Markus Siegl, Michael Buchhold
abstract: Adaptive circuits use measurements and outcome-conditioned feedback to implement nonreciprocal dynamics without postselection. We show that fermion circuits host independently tunable density and coherence skin effects. The stationary state has an exact density tilt set only by measurement strength and feedback displacement: conditioned-gate details cancel, yielding an exponential one-particle profile and, at any filling, a tilted ensemble of configuration weights. Decaying coherences instead obey, in the bulk, an effective Hatano-Nelson generator controlled by the conditioned gates through a relative occupation phase. Tuning this phase drives a point-gap topological transition and reverses coherence localization at fixed density, allowing density and coherence to localize at opposite edges. We derive both exponents for conditioned $U(2)$ gates and propose a correlator-ratio probe using ensemble-averaged observables.
summary: This paper analyzes adaptive fermion circuits to show that density and coherence localization effects can be tuned independently. By analyzing the system's Liouvillian dynamics, the authors derive separate exponents for density and coherence profiles. This separation is significant because it allows for engineered localization of these two distinct physical properties at opposite ends of the chain.
main_problem: To investigate whether density and coherence skin effects can be independently tuned in adaptive fermion circuits, unlike previous models where they were coupled.
main_result: The density skin effect exponent is fixed by measurement strength and feedback displacement, while the coherence exponent can be tuned independently by controlling the relative occupation phase, allowing opposite-edge localization.
method: The analysis uses Liouvillian dynamics, employing gauge transformations and exponential ansatz fitting to extract the decay exponents for both density and coherence profiles.
model_or_system: The system models spinless fermions on a chain evolving under a trace-preserving Liouvillian governed by measurement-feedback updates, $\partial_t \hat{ho} = \mathcal{L}\hat{ho}$.
key_observables: Density skin effect exponent ($\kappa_{	ext{dens}}$), coherence skin effect exponent ($\kappa_{	ext{coh}}$), and the stationary density profile $ho_{n_R}$.
important_parameters: Measurement strength ($	au$), feedback displacement ($d$), and the relative occupation phase ($	heta$).
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes an exponential ansatz for the stationary density state and utilizes gauge transformations to map the non-reciprocal dynamics to a normal form for coherence analysis.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the adaptive measurement-feedback update, showing density and coherence profiles at opposite edges, and plot the dependence of $\kappa_{	ext{coh}}$ and $\kappa_{	ext{dens}}$ on control parameters $	au$ and $	heta$.
paper_structure: The paper first establishes the Liouvillian framework for adaptive circuits, then derives the independent expressions for $\kappa_{	ext{dens}}$ and $\kappa_{	ext{coh}}$, demonstrating their tunability and the mechanism allowing opposite-edge localization.
why_interesting: This work provides a concrete, controllable platform (adaptive circuits) to study the separation of different types of localization effects (density vs. coherence) in open quantum systems, which is highly relevant to understanding dissipation and measurement backaction in quantum dynamics.
